result.description: Hosting and deployment platform for web sites and apps (builds, deploys, functions, DNS, forms).
result.auth_detail: OAuth2 auth-code (app registered in user settings, authorize at app.netlify.com/authorize) for public integrations; personal access token sent as Bearer header for own account.
result.access_detail: Anyone can register an OAuth app in user settings and each user can create a PAT. Docs show no app review/approval step for other users to authorize. Free plan ($0 forever) lists "Deploy from AI, Git, or API"; no paid-plan API restriction found on pricing page. Review step not explicitly ruled out (docs page partially read).
result.api_notes: REST/JSON OpenAPI spec v2.63.1 at api.netlify.com/api/v1. Groups: user accounts, sites, env vars, files, domains/DNS, SNI certs, deploys, builds, dev servers, agent runners, webhooks/notifications, functions, database, forms, split tests, large media, identity.

evidence.quote: If you're making a public integration with Netlify for others to enjoy, you must use OAuth2.
Use your PAT for manual authentication in shell scripts or commands that use the Netlify API.
You can register a new application in your Netlify user settings for OAuth applications.
Deploy from AI, Git, or API.
This is a REST-style API that uses JSON for serialization and OAuth 2 for authentication.
Netlify offers an MCP server, which you can connect to through a connector, plugin, or your agent.
Netlify is a hosting service for the programmable web.
